DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93, Module 5.

These pages are tagged Water-system only: Boilers; Cooling towers; Demineralizers; Pressurizers; Steam traps; Precoat and deep-bed filters. Other pages apply to the sodium and salt systems.

Terminal objective

1.0 Without references, DESCRIBE the purpose, construction, and operation of miscellaneous mechanical components. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

Enabling objectives

1.1 STATE the three common types of air compressors. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

1.2 DESCRIBE the basic operation of the following types of air compressors: DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

  • a. Reciprocating
  • b. Centrifugal
  • c. Rotary

1.3 STATE the reason for using cooling systems in air compressors. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

1.4 STATE three hazards associated with pressurized air systems. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

1.5 Given the appropriate information, CALCULATE the pressure or force achieved in a hydraulic piston. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

1.6 DESCRIBE the basic operation of a hydraulic system. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

1.7 DESCRIBE the basic operation of a boiler. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

1.8 IDENTIFY the following components of a typical boiler: DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

  • a. Steam drum
  • b. Distribution header(s)
  • c. Combustion chamber
  • d. Downcomer
  • e. Risers

1.9 STATE the purpose of cooling towers. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

1.10 DESCRIBE the operation of the following types of cooling towers. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.viii

  • a. Forced draft
  • b. Natural convection

1.11 STATE the purpose of a demineralizer. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.ix

1.12 STATE the four purposes of a pressurizer. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.ix

1.13 DEFINE the following terms attributable to a dynamic pressurizer: DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.ix

  • a. Spray nozzle
  • b. Insurge
  • c. Outsurge
  • d. Surge volume

1.14 STATE the purpose and general operation of a steam trap. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.ix

1.15 IDENTIFY the following types of steam traps: DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.ix

  • a. Ball float steam trap
  • b. Bellow steam trap
  • c. Bucket steam trap
  • d. Impulse steam trap

1.16 DESCRIBE each of the following types of strainers and filters, including an example of typical use. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.ix

  • a. Cartridge filters
  • b. Precoated filters
  • c. Deep-bed filters
  • d. Bucket strainer
  • e. Duplex strainer

1.17 EXPLAIN the application and operation of a strainer or filter backwash. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.ix

Reciprocating compressors

Objectives 1.1, 1.2

"Three types of designs include reciprocating, rotary, and centrifugal air compressors." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.1
"The reciprocating air compressor, illustrated in Figure 1, is the most common design employed today." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.1

The main elements are the compressing element, the rods, crankshaft and flywheel that carry power to the piston, a lubricating system, a regulation system that holds discharge pressure in a set range, and an unloading system that eases the load on the prime mover at start. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.1

On the suction stroke, the piston moves down and the air in the clearance space expands until cylinder pressure falls below the pressure on the other side of the inlet valve. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.3

"This difference in pressure causes the inlet valve to open into the cylinder until the piston reaches the bottom of its stroke (Figure 2C)." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.3

On the compression stroke, the piston moves up and the spring-loaded inlet valve closes. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.3

"As the piston continues upward, air is compressed until the pressure in the cylinder becomes great enough to open the discharge valve against the pressure of the valve springs and the pressure of the discharge line (Figure 2E)." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.3

Objective 1.1Q1508

What are the three common types of air compressors?

The answer is A. The handbook names reciprocating, rotary, and centrifugal designs. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.1

Objective 1.2Q1509

In a reciprocating air compressor, what opens the discharge valve?

The answer is C. Air is compressed until cylinder pressure is great enough to open the discharge valve against the valve springs and the discharge line. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.3

Rotary and centrifugal compressors

Objectives 1.2

"Rotary compressor units are classified into three general groups, slide vane-type, lobe-type, and liquid seal ring-type." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.4

Rotary units are compact, relatively inexpensive, and take a fraction of the space and weight of a reciprocating machine of equal capacity. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.4

"The size of each cell is reduced by the eccentricity of the rotor as the vanes approach the discharge port, thus compressing the air." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.4

The lobe type has two gear-driven mating rotors. The cavity between them shrinks as they rotate, which compresses the vapor until the discharge port is reached. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.5

The liquid seal ring type has an open impeller in an oblong cavity filled with liquid. Centrifugal force throws the seal liquid to the outer edge, and the oblong case makes the cells shrink as the rotor turns. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.5

"The actual compression of the air takes place due either to centrifugal forces or a diminishing air space as the impellers rotate." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9

In a centrifugal compressor, air enters the eye of the impeller and is thrown against the casing. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.6

"The air becomes compressed as more and more air is thrown out to the casing by the impeller blades." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9

Several stages may be used, as in a centrifugal pump, to reach a higher pressure. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.6

"Some of its uses are pneumatic control devices, pneumatic sensors, pneumatic valve operators, pneumatic motors, and starting air for diesel engines." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.6

How does a centrifugal air compressor compress air?

Compressor coolers

Objectives 1.3

Raising air pressure lowers the amount of moisture the air can hold, and raising its temperature raises that amount. The pressure change is the larger effect, so moisture condenses. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.6

"The condensed moisture can cause corrosion, water hammers, and freeze damage; therefore, it is important to avoid moisture in compressed air systems." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.6
"Coolers used on the discharge of a compressor are called aftercoolers." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.7
"If the compressor is multi-staged, there may be an intercooler, which is usually located after the first stage discharge and before the second stage suction." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.7
"Cooling systems are required in compressed air systems to remove any heat added by the compression." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9
"Air coolers are used because drier compressed air helps prevent corrosion and cooler compressed air allows more air to be compressed for a set volume." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.7

Moisture that condenses in the cooler is collected in condensate traps, which are drained automatically or by hand. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.7

Objective 1.3Q1512

Why are cooling systems used on air compressors?

The answer is D. Cooling removes the heat of compression. Drier air helps prevent corrosion, and cooler air allows more air to be compressed for a set volume. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.7

Objective 1.3Q1513

Where is an intercooler usually located on a multi-staged compressor?

The answer is B. An intercooler is usually located after the first stage discharge and before the second stage suction. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.7

Hazards of compressed air

Objectives 1.4

The handbook's summary gives three general hazards. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9

"Small leaks or breaks can cause minute particles to be blown at speeds high enough to cause damage." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9

Safety glasses or goggles should be worn around compressed gas. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9

"Hearing protection should be worn around compressors." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9

Compressors, and the cycling of automatic drain valves, can be quite noisy. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9

"Pressure swings may cause system damage." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9
"Closed valves should be slowly cracked open and both sides should be allowed to equalize prior to opening the valve further." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.8

Systems should be depressurized before they are opened for maintenance. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.8

"Oil introduced in an air compressor can be compressed to the point where detonation takes place in a similar manner as that which occurs in a diesel engine." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.8

That detonation can damage equipment and injure people, so oil is kept out of air systems. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.8

Hydraulic pressure and force

Objectives 1.5

A hydraulic system uses a liquid to develop a force. Oil is the most common choice. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.10

"Oil helps to lubricate the various sliding parts, prevents rust, and is readily available." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.10
"Blaise Pascal discovered that pressure in a fluid acts equally in all directions." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.10
"Pressure is the amount of force on a unit area of the surface." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.10

F = P x A (F in lbf, P in lbf/in.², A in in.²) DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.10

Knowledge check: Hydraulic pressure and force

Objective 1.5Q75

In a hydraulic piston, the force developed equals:

The answer is A. The handbook gives F = P x A for a hydraulic piston, so force is pressure times area and none of the other combinations. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93, Hydraulics, ME-05 p. 13

Report a problem
Objective 1.5Q1516

A hydraulic piston has an area of 4 in.² and the oil pressure is 500 psi. What force is exerted on the piston?

The answer is C. F = P x A = 500 lbf/in.² x 4 in.² = 2000 lbf. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.10

Hydraulic system operation

Objectives 1.6

Oil flows from a tank or reservoir through a pipe into a pump, often through a filter on the pump suction. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.11

"The pump, usually a gear-type, positive displacement pump, can be driven by an electric motor, air motor, gas or steam turbine, or an internal combustion engine." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.11
"The pressure control box shown on Figure 8 is usually a relief valve that provides a means of returning oil to the reservoir upon overpressurization." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.11
"The control valve changes the direction of oil flow, depending upon the desired direction of the load." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.12
"The oil that enters the cylinder applies pressure over the area of the piston, developing a force on the piston rod." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.12

Oil from the other side of the piston returns to the reservoir. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.12

Hydraulic systems carry the hazards of pressurized systems as well as hazards from the fluid itself. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.12

"A severe fire hazard is generated when a break in the high pressure piping occurs and the oil is vaporized into the atmosphere." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.13

In a basic hydraulic system, what does the directional control valve do?

What usually protects a hydraulic system from overpressure?

Boilers

Objectives 1.7, 1.8

"The primary function of a boiler is to produce steam at a given pressure and temperature." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.14

Air is mixed with fuel in a controlled combustion process, and the heat is absorbed by water in the risers. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.14

"The density difference between hot and cold water is the driving force to circulate the water back to the steam drum." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.14

Steam leaves the drum through a baffle that drops out water droplets, and it may pass through a superheater if superheated steam is required. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.14

"The economizer uses heat from the boiler exhaust gasses to raise the temperature of the inlet feedwater." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.15
"The steam drum separates the steam from the heated water." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.16
"Downcomers are the pipes in which the water from the steam drum travels to reach the bottom of the boiler." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.17
"Distribution headers are large pipe headers that carry the water from the downcomers to the risers." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.17
"Risers are the piping or tubes that form the combustion chamber enclosure." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.17
"The combustion chamber is located at the bottom of the boiler and is where the air and fuel mix and burn." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.17

Cooling towers

Objectives 1.9, 1.10

"The cooling tower removes heat from water used in cooling systems within the plant." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.23
"Cooling towers minimize the thermal pollution of the natural water heat sinks and allow the reuse of circulating water." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.18
"The cooling of the water in a cooling tower is accomplished by the direct contact of water and air." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.19

The cooling comes mainly from the latent heat of a small amount of evaporated water, and also from sensible heat that warms the air. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.19

"Induced draft cooling towers use fans to create a draft that pulls air through the cooling tower fill." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.23
"The primary difference is that the air is blown in at the bottom of the tower and exits at the top." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.21
"Water distribution problems and recirculation difficulties discourage the use of forced draft cooling towers." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.21
"Natural convection cooling towers, illustrated in Figure 12, use the principle of convective flow to provide air circulation." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.21
"The air circulation will be self perpetuating due to the density difference between the warmer air inside and the cooler air outside." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.22
"Because of space considerations and cost, natural convection cooling towers are built less frequently than other types." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.22

What sustains the air flow in a natural convection cooling tower?

Demineralizers

Objectives 1.11

"Dissolved impurities in power plant fluid systems generate corrosion problems and decrease efficiency due to fouled heat transfer surfaces." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.24
"Demineralization of the water is one of the most practical and common methods available to remove these dissolved impurities." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.24
"Ion exchangers are generally classified into two groups: single-bed ion exchangers and mixed-bed ion exchangers." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.29

A demineralizer is basically a cylindrical tank that holds resin beads between upper and lower retention elements. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.24

"The water to be purified enters the top at a set flow rate and flows down through the resin beads, where the flow path causes a physical filter effect as well as a chemical ion exchange." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.24
"A mixed-bed demineralizer is a demineralizer in which the cation and anion resin beads are mixed together." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.26

A mixed bed is in effect equal to a number of two-step demineralizers in series, and its water is extremely pure. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.26

"The regeneration of a single-bed ion exchanger is a three-step process." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.25

The chemistry behind these units is taught in CH-04. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.24

"It is important to realize that if the ion exchanger has been exposed to radioactive materials, the backwash, regeneration, and rinse solutions may be highly radioactive and must be treated as a radioactive waste." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.26

Steam traps

Objectives 1.14, 1.15

"Steam traps are installed in steam lines to drain condensate from the lines without allowing the escape of steam." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.35
"A steam trap consists of a valve and a device or arrangement that causes the valve to open and close as necessary to drain the condensate from the lines without allowing the escape of steam." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.39
"Steam traps are installed at low points in the system or machinery to be drained." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.39

In a ball float trap, the valve opens when the float rises. Water lifts the float, the condensate drains, and the float drops and closes the valve before steam can escape. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.35

In a bucket trap, the valve closes as the bucket floats up and stays closed until the bucket fills. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.36

"When the bucket is full, it sinks and thus opens the valve." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.36

A bellows trap is a thermostatic trap. A volatile liquid sealed in the bellows expands when heated by steam. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.36

"The valve is attached to the bellows in such a way that the valve closes when the bellows expands." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.37
"The impulse type of steam trap is dependent on the principle that hot water under pressure tends to flash into steam when the pressure is reduced." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.37
"The only moving part in the steam trap is the disk." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.37
"Orifice-type steam traps are not suitable for services in which the condensate formation is not continuous." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.38

Cartridge filters

Objectives 1.16

"Filtration is a process used to remove suspended solids from a solution." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.40
"In general, the filter passage must be small enough to catch the suspended solids but large enough that the system can operate at normal system pressures and flows." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.40
"The cartridges are cylinders and usually consist of a fiber yarn wound around a perforated metal core." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.40

Porous metal cartridges are used in some high temperature or high pressure applications. Cartridges are made to remove all particles above a set size. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.41

"Cartridge filters have the advantage of being relatively inexpensive to install and operate." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.41

Differential pressure instruments tell the operator when a filter is plugged and must be replaced. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.41

Precoat and deep-bed filters

Objectives 1.16

"A precoat filter eliminates the problem of physically handling radioactive materials, because the filter material (called the medium) can be installed and removed remotely." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.42

Inside the housing is a bundle of septums, the vertical tubes on which the medium is deposited. To precoat the filter, a slurry of medium and demineralized water is recirculated until the water runs clear. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.42

"Because water pressure holds the filter in place, flow must be maintained through the recirculating loop to keep the medium from falling off." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.43
"Filters are usually installed in pairs, so that one filter can remain in service while the other is undergoing the filter backwashing and precoating process." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.43

Precoat filters cost much more and are more complicated than cartridge filters. Their major advantage is remote operation. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.44

"Deep-bed filters are usually found only in makeup water systems, where they are used to filter water after it has been treated in a clarifier." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.44

Water percolates down through a bed of granular anthracite or charcoal on a coarse aggregate layer and a support screen. Charcoal also removes organic matter and chlorine, while anthracite removes only particulates. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.44

Strainers and backwashing

Objectives 1.16, 1.17

"Strainers are fitted in many piping lines to prevent the passage of grit, scale, dirt, and other foreign matter, which could obstruct pump suction valves, throttle valves, or other machinery parts." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.45
"The bucket strainer is literally a bucket to catch debris." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.47

A typical bucket strainer sits in a sump pump suction line. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.45

"A duplex strainer is a strainer consisting of two sides with a basket in each side." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.48

Duplex strainers are common in fuel oil and lubricating oil lines, where flow must not be interrupted. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.45

"The flow may be diverted from one basket to the other, while one is being cleaned." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.45

When a filter or strainer cannot be easily removed for cleaning, the system design usually includes a backwash flowpath. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.46

"The intent of a backwash is to flow liquid in the opposite direction of normal flow, creating a pressure that pushes the debris off the strainer or filter." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.46
"Normally, to establish a backwash lineup, the flowpath upstream of the inlet to the strainer or filter is closed, the flow path downstream of the outlet is closed, and a drain flowpath is opened." DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.46

The flush source is then opened, and flow carries the debris out through the inlet to the drain or waste tank. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.47

Objective 1.16Q1532

Why is a duplex strainer used in fuel oil and lubricating oil lines?

The answer is C. The flow may be diverted from one basket to the other while one is being cleaned, which keeps oil flow uninterrupted. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.45

Report a problem
Objective 1.17Q76

During a backwash of a strainer or filter, liquid flows:

The answer is A. The handbook says a backwash flows liquid opposite to normal flow, and its lineup sends flush water into the outlet and out the inlet to the drain, so normal-direction flow and a bypass are wrong. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93, Filters and Strainers, ME-05 p. 46

Worked examples

Objective 1.5

Force on a hydraulic piston

In a hydraulic system, the oil pressure at the inlet to the cylinder is 1500 psi, and the area of the piston is two square inches. Calculate the force exerted on the piston.

  1. F = P x A
  2. F = 1500 lbf/in.² x 2 in.²

Answer: F = 3000 lbf

DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.11

Objective 1.5

Pressure to open a hydraulic valve

A hydraulic valve requires a force of 1848 lbf to be opened. The piston area is 3 square inches. How much pressure does the hydraulic fluid have to exert?

  1. P = F / A
  2. P = 1848 lbf / 3 in.²

Answer: P = 616 lbf/in.²

DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.11

Summary

  • The three common air compressors are reciprocating, rotary, and centrifugal. Cooling removes the heat of compression, which gives drier air and allows more air in a set volume. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9
  • Compressed air hazards are particles blown from leaks, noise, and pressure swings. Oil must be kept out of air systems. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.9
  • Hydraulic force is F = P x A. A pump raises oil pressure, a control valve directs it, and oil pressure on the piston moves the load. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.13
  • Boilers make steam. The steam drum, downcomers, distribution headers, risers, and combustion chamber are the main parts. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.17
  • Cooling towers remove heat from cooling water and release it to the air, by induced draft, forced draft, or natural convection. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.23
  • Demineralizers remove dissolved impurities from water. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.29
  • Steam traps drain condensate without letting steam escape. Types include ball float, bucket, bellows, and impulse. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.39
  • Filters and strainers remove suspended solids. A backwash reverses flow to push debris to a drain. DOE-HDBK-1018/2-93 ME-05 p.48
